THREAT_MODEL.md T2, line 121, names it in as many words: "**A second residual, on a bound marker, is not a narrower instance of the first — it is the whole sweep, skipped.** `internal/load`'s `recheckWholeTarget` returns immediately when `l.run.MarkerBound` is true ... on that path a table a third party creates in the target strictly after the gate and strictly before the first drop is not caught by anything at gate time or by this sweep, and is loaded around exactly as the round-4 finding above describes, exiting 0." That sentence also records the closure as future work: it needs the gate to answer rule 5 on a bound marker too, and notes the residual has no regression test. The fix this entry proposed still stands and is still unimplemented: on the marker-bound path run the same ProbeEmptiness sweep and, for each occupied table that is neither in the plan nor in the marker's own record of the tables the previous run wrote, print target.warn.unknown_tables naming it and degrade the exit to non-zero rather than refusing (refusing would false-positive on a legitimately full reload target, which TestAMarkerBoundReloadIgnoresATableItsSourceNoLongerHas pins). That requires the marker to record the tables the run wrote — the thing that makes "this database is mine" a checkable claim rather than a single bound row. Note the documented residual is about the operator-facing half only: nothing of production leaked out of the source, and nothing of the target was destroyed; what survives is a green exit over a database that is part fake slice and part somebody else's rows.
